title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 15
statement: A recipe that makes \(5\) servings of hot chocolate requires \(2\) squares of chocolate, \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) cup sugar, \(1\) cup water and \(4\) cups milk. Jordan has \(5\) squares of chocolate, \(2\) cups of sugar, lots of water, and \(7\) cups of milk. If she maintains the same ratio of ingredients, what is the greatest number of servings of hot chocolate she can make?

solutions.text:
We need to find which ingredient is the limiting factor.

Jordan has enough chocolate for \(5\div2=\dfrac{5}{2}\) batches, enough sugar for \(2\div\dfrac{1}{4}=8\) batches, and enough milk for \(7\div4=\dfrac{7}{4}\) batches.

The milk is limiting, so Jordan can make \(5\cdot\dfrac{7}{4}=\dfrac{35}{4}=8\dfrac{3}{4}\) servings.

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Compare how many recipe batches each ingredient can support.
The ingredient that supports the fewest batches limits the servings.
